FinishReason.description:
Normalized finish-reason signal indicating why a generation stopped.

Each provider's native stop value is mapped to one of these, and the unmapped original string is preserved in `rawFinishReason` as an escape hatch. `null` means the provider did not emit a finish_reason (e.g. the stream was cut off before the final event).

- `'completed'`: normal completion (OpenAI `'stop'`, Anthropic   `'end_turn'` / `'stop_sequence'`, Gemini `'STOP'`).
- `'tool_calls'`: generation paused so the caller can dispatch tool   calls and feed their results back. Note that the OpenAI Responses API   and Google GenAI report `'completed'` here; only the Chat   Completions–style providers and Anthropic surface a dedicated value.
- `'truncated'`: token budget exhausted (OpenAI `'length'`, Anthropic   `'max_tokens'`, Gemini `'MAX_TOKENS'`, Responses `'max_output_tokens'`).
- `'filtered'`: content filter or safety policy blocked the response.
- `'paused'`: Anthropic-specific `'pause_turn'`.
- `'other'`: recognized non-null reason that does not fit the categories   above.

The structure passed across process / language boundaries (RPC, events, telemetry, SDK wrappers). Class identity does not survive the boundary; downstream code must branch on `code` rather than `instanceof`.

GoalSnapshot.description: Public, computed view of the current goal.

GoalStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a goal — deliberately minimal. The durable record only ever holds `active`, `paused`, or `blocked`; `complete` is transient (announce-then-clear) and never rests on disk. There is exactly one running state, two resumable "stopped" states, and one success outcome:

| Status     | Persisted | Resumable | Set by                          | Meaning                                          | |------------|-----------|-----------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------| | `active`   | yes       | (running) | createGoal / resumeGoal         | The goal driver may run continuation turns.      | | `paused`   | yes       | yes       | pauseGoal / pauseActiveGoal /   | User, interrupt, resume, or retryable runtime    | |            |           |           | pauseOnInterrupt /              | stop parked it; intact.                          | |            |           |           | normalizeMetadata               |                                                  | | `blocked`  | yes       | yes       | markBlocked                     | The system stopped it for some `reason`.         | | `complete` | no        | —         | markComplete                    | Success — announced in a message, then cleared.  |

Only an `active` goal advances: accounting and continuation turns all gate on `status === 'active'`. `paused` and `blocked` are the same kind of thing — "the driver is not running continuation turns, but the goal is intact and resumable via `/goal resume`" — differing only in *who* stopped it (the user vs the system) and the human-readable `reason`. There is no separate `impossible`, `budget_limited`, `error`, or `cancelled` status: an unachievable goal, an exhausted budget, or a non-retryable runtime failure becomes `blocked(+reason)`, retryable runtime stops become `paused(+reason)`, and `cancelGoal` discards the record entirely. See  {@link  SessionGoalStore }  for the setters and the per-status notes below.

GoalActor.description: Who performed a goal action. `cleared` is an audit action, not a status.

GoalBudgetReport.description: Computed budget view exposed through snapshots and tools.

role.description: The role of the message sender.

content.description: Ordered content parts (text, images, thinking, etc.).

toolCalls.description: Tool calls requested by the assistant in this message.

toolCallId.description: For `tool` role messages, the ID of the tool call this result answers.

partial.description: When `true`, indicates the message was not fully received (e.g. stream interrupted).

coalescedCount.description: Number of theoretical fires that were collapsed into this single delivery (>= 1).

stale.description: True for recurring tasks past the 7-day age threshold.

count.description: Number of one-shot tasks bundled into this missed-fire notification.

ContentPart.description:
A single piece of content within a  {@link  Message } .

The union covers text, model reasoning ("think"), images, audio, and video. Providers convert these to their native content-block format during  {@link  ChatProvider.generate  } .

_streamIndex.description: Provider-specific streaming index used to route argument deltas to the correct parallel tool call. Set by streaming providers (OpenAI Chat Completions `index`, Responses API `item_id`). Consumed internally by  {@link  generate  }  and stripped before the ToolCall is stored on a Message.

stream.description: Use streaming API. Defaults to true. Set to false for non-streaming (test/fallback).

adaptiveThinking.description: Explicitly declare whether the model supports adaptive thinking (`thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }`), overriding the model-name version inference. Useful for custom-named endpoints whose model name does not encode a parseable Claude version. Leave undefined to infer from the name.

ToolMessageConversion.description:
Strategy for converting tool-role message content.

- `'extract_text'`: flatten all content parts into a single text string   (some providers require tool results as plain text).
- `null`: convert content parts to the standard OpenAI content-part array.

max_tokens.description: Legacy completion-budget alias. The Moonshot Kimi API still accepts `max_tokens`, but for reasoning models it shares the budget with `reasoning_content` and a small value can cause a 200 response with no `content`. Prefer `max_completion_tokens`. When both are set `max_completion_tokens` wins; this provider normalizes by sending only `max_completion_tokens` on the wire.

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens the model is expected to emit in a single completion. `0` means the ceiling is unknown.

ModelCapability.description:
Declared capabilities for a specific model exposed by a  {@link  ChatProvider  } .

Providers return one of these from  {@link  ChatProvider.getCapability  }  so callers can gate requests against modalities the model does not accept without dispatching the request and watching it fail upstream.

`max_context_tokens: 0` means "unknown"; callers that do not gate on context length can ignore the field. `max_output_tokens: 0` means "unknown"; callers that do not gate on output length can ignore the field.

PermissionMode.description:
Top-level user-facing permission posture. Controls how non-deny rules are treated when the closure is constructed. Independent of rule merging: deny rules always fire regardless of mode.

  - `manual` — rule set drives decision; unmatched tool calls ask   - `yolo`   — only deny rules can block; everything else allows   - `auto`   — caller may bypass rule checks entirely

PermissionRule.description: A single permission rule. `pattern` is the DSL form (`Read(/etc/**)`, `Bash(rm *)`, or bare `Write`). Rule arguments are interpreted only by tools that provide a matcher; other tools match by name only.

PermissionRuleScope.description: Rule provenance. `session-runtime` stores rules produced by "approve for session"; `turn-override`, `project`, and `user` are reserved for static-loaded rules surfaced by external callers.

ok.description: false when the reviewer could not run or its output was unusable.

escalate.description: Whether this finding must be escalated to the human (severity × audit level × confidence).

See  {@link  SessionGoalStore }  for the setters and the per-status notes below.

ToolMessageConversion.description:
Strategy for converting tool-role message content.

- `'extract_text'`: flatten all content parts into a single text string   (some providers require tool results as plain text).
- `null`: convert content parts to the standard OpenAI content-part array.

max_tokens.description: Legacy completion-budget alias. The Moonshot Kimi API still accepts `max_tokens`, but for reasoning models it shares the budget with `reasoning_content` and a small value can cause a 200 response with no `content`. Prefer `max_completion_tokens`. When both are set `max_completion_tokens` wins; this provider normalizes by sending only `max_completion_tokens` on the wire.

thinkingBudget.description: Indicates the thinking budget in tokens. 0 is DISABLED. -1 is AUTOMATIC. The default values and allowed ranges are model dependent.

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens the model is expected to emit in a single completion. `0` means the ceiling is unknown.

ModelCapability.description:
Declared capabilities for a specific model exposed by a  {@link  ChatProvider  } .

Providers return one of these from  {@link  ChatProvider.getCapability  }  so callers can gate requests against modalities the model does not accept without dispatching the request and watching it fail upstream.

`max_context_tokens: 0` means "unknown"; callers that do not gate on context length can ignore the field. `max_output_tokens: 0` means "unknown"; callers that do not gate on output length can ignore the field.

PermissionMode.description:
Top-level user-facing permission posture. Controls how non-deny rules are treated when the closure is constructed. Independent of rule merging: deny rules always fire regardless of mode.

  - `manual` — rule set drives decision; unmatched tool calls ask   - `yolo`   — only deny rules can block; everything else allows   - `auto`   — caller may bypass rule checks entirely

PermissionRule.description: A single permission rule. `pattern` is the DSL form (`Read(/etc/**)`, `Bash(rm *)`, or bare `Write`). Rule arguments are interpreted only by tools that provide a matcher; other tools match by name only.

PermissionRuleScope.description: Rule provenance. `session-runtime` stores rules produced by "approve for session"; `turn-override`, `project`, and `user` are reserved for static-loaded rules surfaced by external callers.
